summary.headline: Vibhor Steel guides ~20% Q1 revenue growth, driven by Jharsuguda; Q1 pipe dispatch only 1,500 t against 1,800 t pipe order book.
summary.overview:
Management said Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 20% YoY, with growth coming almost entirely from the Jharsuguda (Odisha) plant, while Mumbai and Hyderabad were broadly flat versus last year. Order books for pipe, crash barrier, transmission line towers (TLT) and poles were described as well above normal, but the second galvanizing tank at Jharsuguda (expected around 1 September) is the binding constraint. Management said new-product contribution would start in Q2 and smooth out in Q3 and Q4. Figures on EBITDA, PAT and margins were not quantified in the call; the company also said it is planning a North India plant via a newly incorporated subsidiary, starting with crash barrier.</overview>

segments.name: Pipe (ERW black/galvanized)
segments.commentary: 83% of revenue. Jharsuguda pipe order book 1,800 t vs ~1,500 t dispatched in Q1; Mumbai order book 6,500 t (1,000 t on hold, ~5,000 t sold); Hyderabad pipe/galv orders ~2,000 t vs 1,000-1,200 t historical average.

segments.name: Crash barrier / highway guardrail
segments.commentary: 12% of revenue. Jharsuguda order book ~600 t and Hyderabad ~850-1,000 t; Jharsuguda crash barrier line is at maximum installed capacity, with another crash barrier line being installed.

segments.name: Transmission line towers (TLT)
segments.commentary: Order book ~2,000 t (MP ~1,500 t, Chhattisgarh 200-250 t, Maharashtra 50-60 t, plus Sikkim, Chennai). Installed capacity ~600-700 t/month; dispatch of 300-400 t expected in the current month. Power Grid approval (~2 months) pending.

segments.name: Poles (octagonal, high-mast)
segments.commentary: Order book ~250 t, equal to ~75-80% of pole installed capacity of 300 t/month. Last 3 months' max sales 80 t; targets 100 t this month, 200 t next month, 300 t by October.

segments.name: Other / RSJ pole / Monopole
segments.commentary: RSJ pole first order ~500 t, processed as job work with ~Rs 1 crore revenue; Monopole certification pending, expected Q3. Monopole has highest margin per management.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27: management expects ~20% revenue growth to continue plus incremental ~1,000 t/month (~Rs 10 crore/month, ~30%) from TLT, poles and crash barrier; said 20-25% growth expected through the year, with the new products yet to contribute meaningfully.

Second galvanizing tank at Jharsuguda expected to be operational around 1 September; management said it would add at least 1,000-1,500 t of galvanizing capacity and roughly Rs 100-150 crore of revenue (rough estimate, as stated).
Growth from new products expected to start in Q2 and smooth out in Q3 and Q4.
North India plant: land purchase in talks; new subsidiary created for the plant, first phase crash barrier; management did not give capex amount or commissioning date.
Capex: management said further capex depends on utilisation; no FY27 capex quantum given.
capex_capacity: Jharsuguda: second galvanizing tank expected to be commissioned around 1 September 2026 (monsoon delay of ~2 weeks); one more crash barrier line being installed (bought last year).
Jharsuguda pole capacity ~300 t/month, effectively maxed out; TLT installed capacity ~600-700 t/month, could rise to ~2,000 t with Power Grid orders.
Sundargarh total capacity 1,56,000 t per annum (~40,000 t per quarter per management); utilisation ~18% overall.
North India plant under planning via new subsidiary; land purchase under discussion, not finalised.
Future Jharsuguda galvanizing tanks to be dedicated by product (pipe, crash barrier, TLT, RSJ, poles); timing not fixed.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand strong during monsoon; management cites government infrastructure push, high freight costs for imports and steel makers focusing on domestic sales.
Management is turning away export orders (EN10255/EN10217 galvanized), 1161/3601 BIS orders and hollow section orders because galvanizing tanks are full and margins are thin.
Product margin ranking per management: Monopole > TLT > pole > crash barrier (~3%) > pipe; some TLT and pole orders reportedly gave ~10% margin, overall ~2%.
Pipe orders arriving at ~100 t/day in Mumbai per management; dealer-MOU based allocation prioritised over end users.
Management said competition in TLT and poles is limited for 2-3 years due to engineering and certification requirements.
